Bug_Title: NP: Null value is guaranteed to be dereferenced (NP_GUARANTEED_DEREF)
Bug_Details:
There is a statement or branch that if executed guarantees that
      a value is null at this point, and that
      value that is guaranteed to be dereferenced
      (except on forward paths involving runtime exceptions).
       Note that a check such as
    if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException();
    is treated as a dereference of x. if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException(); x
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by ensuring that the variable'result' is explicitly set to null when the input is null. The subsequent call to'result.toUpperCase()' will guarantee a NullPointerException because'result' is guaranteed to be null.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method with a null input, which guarantees that the'result' variable is set to null. The subsequent call to'result.toUpperCase()' triggers a NullPointerException.
